report:
PASS for the stated restricted logarithmic-reference selection and stability theorems. original_programme_closed=false. The result satisfies the completion criterion allowing a new singular-reference/varying-data regime. H remains continuous and positive; this does not establish selection for arbitrary L1 densities or arbitrary model references.

I independently checked the final article, the historical arguments, and notes n1–n8. Previous verdicts, source-reading declarations, hashes, candidate flags and numerical observations were not used as mathematical premises. The external premises below were checked against freshly opened primary sources.

1. Geometry and normalization. The horizontal and vertical blocks make θ and η strictly positive. Nonconstant b makes db∧κ nonzero, independently of dκ; horizontal degrees prevent cancellation. Thus neither background is closed. The volume dW has mass one. With the specified operator, dd^c log|t|²=δ₀, so θ+dd^cψ=η+d[D], with the genuine value −∞ on D. These calculations establish the required hypotheses directly; positivity, bigness and nefness are not inferred from a note.

2. Divisorial removal. From v≤ψ+C, the residual r=v−ψ is bounded above off D and is η-psh there. Adding a closed dominating quadratic gives a psh function to which removability applies. The subsequent positivity argument is valid: η+dd^cr has measure coefficients, is positive off D, and its restriction to D is the restriction of the positive corrected Hessian, because smooth forms assign D zero measure. This proves positivity across D without incorrectly subtracting a smooth form from a positive current. Canonical representatives give uniqueness and genuine equality, including the common poles. Bounded type is equivalent to a bounded residual. The product identity follows from bounded corrected algebra on common finite levels off D and exhaustion; both genuine non-pluripolar measures omit D. This argument also accommodates additional poles and possibly infinite competitor mass.

3. The ordinary model. The tangent point is exactly |z|²=a/d. The exterior profile has value and first derivative zero at that circle. Its bounded residual F=φ−ψ, interpreted through its explicit extension rather than subtraction of infinities, increases from 0 to C*. The horizontal current is K·1_{|z|²<R}ω₁+d[p]; its non-pluripolar horizontal mass is K R/(1+R)=a. Matching derivatives exclude a boundary-circle atom. The convex-envelope proof is sound. The independent exterior-disk maximum-principle proof gives the same upper bound.

For every product competitor, adding K times a local horizontal Fubini–Study potential and a sufficiently large vertical quadratic makes it psh. Restricting this correction to a horizontal slice retains precisely Kω₁. Every slice is therefore a curve competitor or identically −∞. This proves the product envelope bound without symmetry of Y. The lifted φ attains the bound, and bounded comparison between φ and ψ gives Pθ[φ](0)=φ. The smaller-background assertion also has an established antecedent: δK>d makes ψ δθ-psh and ψ≤φ. A local envelope is then bounded between this competitor and φ. The additional identity Pη(−ψ)=F in n3 follows by converting each residual competitor into a θ-psh competitor below zero.

4. Greatestness against the full singular class. The bounded existence application has all its hypotheses: η is smooth and strictly positive, its minimal potential is zero, a constant is a strict analytic barrier, and gσ=exp(σψ)f is nonnegative, bounded, nonzero and continuous. Its zeros on D are allowed. Section 4 explicitly dispenses with a bounded mass assumption. [BGL §4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.01090v1)

For arbitrary residual r, tM=max(r,Rσ−M) is bounded. Choose a fixed truncation level −j strictly below the entire floor. On its selected residual branch, bounded truncation locality identifies the actual non-pluripolar measure; on the floor branch, the solution measure dominates the required exponential density. The ordered maximum inequality includes the equality set. On {Rσ<tM−ε}, the resulting measure ratio is exp(−σε)<1. Both compared potentials are bounded, their difference is bounded, and a sufficiently negative constant barrier lies below both. Strict domination gives Rσ≥tM−ε and hence Rσ≥r. There is no application of an unjustified comparison theorem to unbounded potentials. Bounded comparison in both directions proves uniqueness in ordinary bounded type. The negative-constant truncation route in n5 is independently valid and reaches the same conclusion. [Guedj–Lu Lemma 1.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2106.04272), [bounded exponential comparison](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2107.01938v1)

5. Construction and actual measures. The contraction preserves a fixed mean-zero sup-norm ball once σ is sufficiently small. The claimed density bound follows by requiring exp(2σR₀)≤2. Differentiating the normalized density gives the displayed derivative and Lipschitz constant 2σBCG. Thus the uniform residual bound is additive and established before taking limits.

The fixed point has continuous distributional complex Hessian Aσω₁. Corrected local Bedford–Taylor mollification identifies its actual product. Bidegrees leave precisely one horizontal factor, yielding N b^k Aσ dW. For the model’s bounded residual, the same curve-dependent approximation proves the formula despite the jump of its horizontal density at the tangent circle. No divisor current is squared. The mass is finite and positive; indeed it lies between N a(min b)^k and N a(max b)^k.

6. Independent Green/barrier reconstruction. The Fubini–Study pushforward by ℓ is uniform on [0,1]. Consequently ∫−logℓ=1 and ∫(−logℓ)²=2. The Green normalization, CG=2/e and ∫G²=1 follow directly. Uniform logarithmic tails prove continuity of bounded-density convolution and the stated L1-to-uniform upgrade under a common density bound.

The all-exponent curve existence route also has a correct normalization: Nguyen’s operator is twice the task’s operator. Taking source background 2σaω₁, unknown U=σq and relative density Hℓ^{σd}/a gives precisely the claimed curve equation. Its nonnegative density is nonzero although it vanishes at the pole. The two Green barriers are respectively a subsolution and a supersolution. Their comparison gives a uniform bound for qσ−σ⁻¹log c₀. The subsequent Taylor estimate is valid even where the logarithm is arbitrarily negative, since its remainder is bounded by σ(dL+B)²exp(σB)/2. This independently recovers the contraction route’s selected residual and constant. [Nguyen Theorem 2.1 and Lemma 2.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.00891v1)

7. Whole-family limits and scalar error. The contraction bound first implies Zσ→m and Aσ→aH/m without presupposing convergence of wσ: exp(σwσ)→1 uniformly, while exp(σψ)→1 almost everywhere. The Green estimate then forces wσ→w₀ uniformly. Supremum convergence follows, giving v₀=ψ+w₀−S₀ in L1 and locally uniformly off D. Its actual measure is c₀f dW, with mass N(a/m)∫b^kHω₁>0.

The exact identity cσ=a exp(σSσ)/Zσ and the dominated difference quotient establish the asserted first-order scalar error. Negative parts are controlled by H(|ψ|+R₀), and positive parts by a constant. Thus sσ−σ⁻¹log c₀ converges to s₀=ψ+w₀−M, where M=∫(ψ+w₀)dν₀. The error tends to S₀−M; it has not been discarded or inferred merely from scalar convergence.

8. Selected potential and reference class. Since v₀ has bounded residual relative to ψ and ψ~φ, its actual ordinary bounded type is φ. For every real t≥1, the explicitly constructed a_t=φ−tC satisfies the stretching inequality. This establishes E_env membership directly, including common poles, without using an unrestricted converse from envelope equality. Positive-exponent densities have their genuine value zero on D; no reciprocal weight or divisor mass enters the equation.

For a separated critical subsolution, the actual horizontal non-pluripolar measure dominates A₀ω₁, whose mass is a. The entire positive horizontal current has mass a by distributional Stokes. Its degree-one non-pluripolar part is its restriction to the finite locus, so domination forces equality and leaves no polar remainder. Consequently dd^c(r−w₀)=0, and canonical harmonic uniqueness gives r=w₀+C. The mean constraint is exactly C≤−M; its greatest member is s₀. Supremum normalization instead gives the unique separated member v₀. This is a proved intrinsic order characterization within the explicitly specified sector, not universal zero-exponent uniqueness. [BEGZ §1.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674)

9. New maximal-coefficient argument. Its hypothetical antecedent is checked rather than treated as granted. If a genuine u=ψ+r satisfies MAθ(u)≥c f dW, B=sup r is finite. For each σ>0, u+σ⁻¹log c−B is an exponential subsolution because exp(σ(ψ+r−B))≤1. Full-class greatestness bounds it by sσ. There exists a point off D where r is finite. Evaluating there and using the already proved bounded centered residual gives log c≤log c₀ after multiplication by σ and passage to zero. The explicit v₀ attains c₀. Additional poles and infinite competitor mass do not invalidate any step.

10. Moving parameters. Positivity and convergence supply uniform tail bounds for a_j,d_j,H_j. The contraction constants do not involve derivatives of b_j. Hence the proof remains valid under uniform convergence of b_j alone. Dominated convergence gives A_j→A₀ in L1, then Green convolution gives uniform residual convergence. The lower bound on d_j and a common residual bound keep all maximizing points away from D, establishing convergence of the moving suprema.

The explicit bounded extensions F_{a_j,d_j} converge uniformly, including the moving tangent circles and infinity. Together with ψ_j=d_j logℓ, this identifies both the reference limit and the limit potential’s ordinary type. The argument does not assume bounded comparisons between references with different logarithmic coefficients. Uniform convergence of b_j and L1 convergence of A_j give total-variation convergence of the actual measures. The difference quotient uses m_j, not m, and has a common integrable dominating function. Thus the asserted scalar error and centered limit require no relation between parameter rates and exponent rates.

11. Nontrivial examples. For a=1,d=1/4,b=2+t,H=1, direct integration gives w₀=S₀=0, M=−1/4, v₀=ψ and s₀=ψ+1/4. The moving choice a_j=1+√σ_j makes limiting-scalar centering diverge by log(1+√σ_j)/σ_j, whereas parameter-specific centering converges. The Hopf quotient is compact and diffeomorphic to S¹×S³. Its displayed positive form descends, its square integral is 16π²log2, and the normalization in n7 is correct. Both non-Kähler arguments work: H²=0 with Stokes, or odd b₁ with Kähler parity. The selected threefold mass is exactly 13.

12. Corrections and scope. The final article correctly supplies the θ-psh hypothesis omitted from the historical removal lemma’s abbreviated statement, explicitly requires positive moving model parameters, and defines the bounded extensions of φ_j−ψ_j at common poles. These are harmless clarifications of hypotheses already used by the proofs. The unsupported numerical GL3 convention factor in raw n1 must be replaced by the submission’s convention-covariant rescaling u↦u/γ and σ↦γσ; no theorem changes. The parity citation is VI.8.5 and VI.8.12, not VI Corollary 8.3. BGL’s intermediate local-maximum display must use vε in the global comparison obtained from the maximum; the needed inequality is independently supplied by the correctly oriented GL2 maximum principle.

The numerical and artifact records in n7–n8 are ancillary, not proofs. The substantive conclusion is the specified singular-reference family with continuous factored data and arbitrary fixed Hermitian second factor. It extends beyond the task’s already resolved minimal-ordinary-type cases because θ is strictly positive while the prescribed references retain genuine logarithmic poles. No unrestricted programme closure, arbitrary-L1 selection, arbitrary-reference stability, or nonseparated critical uniqueness follows.

passages.statement: If A is a closed pluripolar subset of a complex manifold M, every psh function on M\A locally bounded above near A extends uniquely to a psh function on M (Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, I.5.24).

On a domain Ω⊂C^n, every real distribution with positive distributional complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable psh representative. Conversely, a psh function not identically −∞ on any connected component has positive complex Hessian (Demailly I.5.8).
For a nonempty locally uniformly upper-bounded family of psh functions on Ω⊂C^n, its usc supremum is psh and equals its pointwise supremum almost everywhere (Demailly I.5.7).

For locally bounded psh functions on Ω⊂C^n, mixed Bedford–Taylor products are positive closed currents with measure coefficients, are symmetric and multilinear, are defined by the bounded recursion, and converge weakly under decreasing sequences whose limits remain locally bounded (Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2).

Let θ be a smooth semipositive real (1,1)-form, possibly nonclosed, and u,v bounded θ-psh functions on an open subset of a compact complex manifold. Then MAθ(max(u,v)) equals MAθ(u) on {u>v} and dominates 1_{u>v}MAθ(u)+1_{u≤v}MAθ(v). If u≥v, then 1_{u=v}MAθ(u)≥1_{u=v}MAθ(v) (Guedj–Lu, Quasi-plurisubharmonic envelopes 2, Lemma 1.2).

Let h be a smooth strictly positive real (1,1)-form on a connected compact complex manifold, and u,v bounded h-psh functions. If 1_{u<v}MAh(u)≤τ1_{u<v}MAh(v) for a constant τ∈[0,1), then u≥v. No bounded mass hypothesis is required (bounded positive-background specialization of Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Volumes of Bott–Chern classes, Lemma 4.2).

For a smooth strictly positive real (1,1)-form h on a connected compact complex manifold, a smooth positive volume dV, nonnegative nonzero g∈Lp(dV), p>1, and λ>0, there exists a unique bounded h-psh R satisfying MAh(R)=exp(λR)g dV. No bounded mass hypothesis is required (Boucksom–Guedj–Lu Theorem 4.5; also the strictly positive specialization of Guedj–Lu, Quasi-plurisubharmonic envelopes 3, Theorem 3.4).

For a smooth strictly positive real (1,1)-form h on a connected compact complex manifold, a smooth positive volume dV, nonnegative nonzero g∈Lp(dV), p>1, and λ>0, there exists a unique bounded h-psh R satisfying MAh(R)=exp(λR)g dV.
